name: Central African Republic armed-group conflict
started: 2025-07-11 (current phase: Chad-mediated UPC and 3R disarmament deals; civil war since 2012)
summary: After a decade of civil war, the CAR government, propped up by Wagner and Africa Corps, struck Chad-mediated disarmament deals with the UPC and 3R rebels in July 2025 and re-elected President Touadera in December 2025. Violence has shifted to the southeast, where the Azande militia AAKG, once Wagner-trained, clashed with government forces in Haut-Mbomou in January 2026. It is a lower-intensity war than its neighbours, but the far southeast remains unstable and the Russian security model there is a template for the Sahel.

sides.name: Government and allies
members: Russian forces: Wagner Group and Africa Corps
Azande Ani Kpi Gbe militia (formerly Wagner-trained ally, now partly hostile)
backers: Russia (Wagner remains the main force, regime protection, resource concessions)
sides.strength: Russian personnel about 1,500 mercenaries (2025) per Wikipedia infobox, which also lists 1,500-2,000 Africa Corps; MINUSCA about 14,000 military (2025, attribution unclear in source).

sides.name: Armed groups
members: Remnants of the Coalition of Patriots for Change (CPC)
UPC and 3R holdouts (both signed disarmament deals in July 2025)
Azande Ani Kpi Gbe (AAKG) in Haut-Mbomou, at odds with the government since the 2025 UPC deal
backers: No state backer documented in sources found
sides.strength: AAKG 1,000+ (Wikipedia); no figures for other groups.

background: The CAR collapsed into war in 2012-13 when the mostly Muslim Seleka coalition took Bangui and anti-balaka militias retaliated. Since 2018 Russia's Wagner Group has been Touadera's guarantor, beating back the CPC rebel coalition in 2021 and receiving mining concessions. Moscow has pushed for Wagner to be replaced by the state-run Africa Corps, but as of August 2026 Wagner had kept its position.

In Haut-Mbomou, the Azande Ani Kpi Gbe militia (founded 2023, also called 'Wagner Ti Azande') fought the Fulani-led UPC; it saw the government's 2025 deal with the UPC as betrayal. Why it matters: CAR shows both the durability and the costs of a Russian-run security model (regime survival, mining access, abuse allegations) that the Sahel juntas have copied.
year: Opposition parties boycotted the 28 Dec 2025 general election; Touadera won a third term with 77.9% (Constitutional Court, 19 Jan 2026) on 52.4% turnout, and the African Union said voting was peaceful except in Haut-Mbomou. AAKG fighters clashed with government forces in Haut-Mbomou in January 2026. Legislative and local runoffs were held on 26 Apr 2026. In justice, the Special Criminal Court began the in-absentia trial of ex-president Francois Bozize on 16 June 2026, and the ICC convicted former Seleka commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani of crimes against humanity on 23 Sept 2026.
situation: As of late October 2026 Bangui and the main towns are under government and Russian protection, the UPC and 3R are formally disarming, and the main hotspot is Haut-Mbomou in the southeast, where the AAKG, UPC remnants and the army contest the Zemio-Mboki-Obo area near South Sudan. Data on violence in 2026 is sparse in the sources retrieved.
technical: UPC and 3R signed disarmament agreements on 11 July 2025, mediated and guaranteed by Chad, committing to 'totally disarm, dissolve and reintegrate' (Wikipedia).
Wagner, not Africa Corps, remains the main Russian force in CAR as of August 2026, providing regime security and involved in resource exploitation (Wikipedia, Africa Corps).
AAKG (Azande Ani Kpi Gbe) was trained by Wagner from March to May 2024; about 100 members joined FACA; its integration was suspended after the 2025 UPC deal (Wikipedia).
AAKG is headquartered at Bambouti and active in Haut-Mbomou and Mbomou; it is alleged to have joined Azande-Balanda fighting in South Sudan's Western Equatoria in Feb 2025 (Wikipedia).
Election security: 58 voter registration centres were still closed by violence in Feb 2025; the AU singled out Haut-Mbomou as the only area of election-day violence (Wikipedia).
Accountability: ICC conviction of ex-Seleka commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani (23 Sept 2026) and the in-absentia trial of Bozize at the Special Criminal Court (from 16 June 2026).
casualties: No 12-month fatality figure found in the sources retrieved. Intensity 'medium' is an estimate based on persistent armed-group activity in the southeast and CAR's historical levels; it could be lower given the 2025 disarmament deals.
displaced: More than 1.1 million people have fled their homes in a country of about 5 million (Wikipedia, undated figure).

timeline.event: UPC and 3R sign Chad-mediated disarmament agreements.
Constitutional Court confirms Touadera's re-election with 77.9%.
In-absentia trial of ex-president Bozize opens at the Special Criminal Court.
ICC convicts ex-Seleka commander Mahamat Said Abdel Kani.

outlook: Watch whether UPC and 3R disarmament holds, AAKG-government relations in Haut-Mbomou, spillover from South Sudan and Sudan, and whether Russia finally swaps Wagner for Africa Corps.
